summary: The case against you: {prosecutor} has opened a case about you, your campaign's money or what you kept, and it will run for years.
realLife: One life: He was indicted in 2011 over more than $1 million from backers used to hide his affair during the 2008 race. In 2012 the jury found him not guilty on one count and deadlocked on the rest, and the government dropped the case. Another: In May 2024 a New York jury convicted him on 34 felony counts over payments booked as business expenses; he won the election that fall and was sentenced to an unconditional discharge. The federal cases were dropped after his win. Another: A secret inquiry into whether his recall campaign coordinated with outside groups ran for years under a gag order until Wisconsin's supreme court ended it in 2015.
